agenda.topic: Confirm central paper claims and map each claim to minimum required evidence across portability, signed package integrity, runtime compatibility, and reference-agent usefulness.
Agree on the essential evaluation matrix: environments, baselines, metrics, trial counts, success criteria, ablations, and failure-recovery tests for Meeting Agenda and Literature Review.

Review implementation readiness, including signing and tamper detection, malformed-package rejection, installation and execution across supported environments, runtime reliability, and reproducibility from a clean setup.
Select required paper revisions covering methodology, architecture, security assumptions and limitations, related work, reproducibility instructions, results tables or figures, and scope boundaries.
Assign submission-critical tasks, owners, completion dates, dependencies, fallback plans, and the final acceptance checklist for deciding whether to submit or cut lower-value work.

decisions: Which claims are submission-critical and the minimum experiment or implementation evidence required for each.
Which environments, baselines, metrics, trial counts, ablations, and failure cases will constitute the final evaluation.
Which security, portability, runtime, and clean-environment reproducibility checks must pass before submission.
Which paper sections, figures, tables, limitations, and reproducibility details must be revised.
The owner, deadline, dependency, and fallback plan for every submission-critical task, plus the cutoff for dropping optional work.
goal: Agree on the final set of experiments and paper revisions required before submission, identify the highest-priority remaining tasks, and leave the meeting with a concrete action plan.
preparation_items: Research Lead: bring the current claim list, draft paper, architecture description, and a claim-to-evidence matrix.
Systems Engineer: report supported environments and runtime versions, current package verification behavior, known failure modes, and reproducibility gaps.
Evaluation Lead: bring existing results, candidate baselines, proposed metrics, trial counts, and a list of missing experiments or ablations.
All participants: identify one essential task that could block submission and one lower-value task that can be deferred.
questions: What is the latest date on which each essential experiment can produce usable results for the paper?
Which baseline or ablation can be removed if time or compute becomes constrained without weakening the central claims?
Are any security or portability claims broader than the implemented evidence, requiring narrower wording?
What result or implementation failure would trigger a change in the paper’s claims or a submission deferral?
Who will independently reproduce the final reference-agent workflow, and what evidence will be recorded?
